examples.en: The ramen water boiled over and made the stove dirty.
The milk will boil over, so turn the heat down.
I didn't notice until the soup was boiling over.

examples.ko: 냄비 뚜껑을 살짝 열어 두면 덜 끓어넘쳐요.
examples.en: If you leave the pot lid slightly open, it boils over less.
The porridge boiled over and spilled on the floor.
Even when my anger felt ready to boil over, I held it in.

explain: 요리할 때 국이나 우유, 라면 물이 끓으면서 냄비 밖으로 넘치는 상황에 많이 써요. '끓어오르다'는 끓으면서 위로 올라오는 것까지만 말하고, 끓어넘치다는 밖으로 넘치는 것을 말해요. 감정이 매우 커진 모습에 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in cooking, when soup, milk, or ramen water boils and spills out of the pot. '끓어오르다' means the liquid only rises up while boiling, while '끓어넘치다' means it spills out. It can also be used figuratively for strong emotions.

examples.en: The lamb has a gamey smell.
To get rid of the gamey smell, add ginger.
This meat is tender with no gamey smell.

examples.ko: 노린내에 민감한 사람은 이 요리를 싫어해요.
examples.en: People who are sensitive to gamey smells dislike this dish.

examples.ko: 염소 고기는 노린내 때문에 호불호가 갈려요.
examples.en: Goat meat divides people because of its gamey smell.

examples.ko: 노린내도 거의 안 나서 먹을 만했어요.
examples.en: It hardly had any gamey smell, so it was good enough to eat.

explain: 양고기나 염소 고기처럼 짐승 고기에서 나는 특유의 냄새예요. 생선이나 날것에서 나는 냄새는 '비린내'라고 해서 구분해요. 요리할 때 '노린내를 잡다'처럼 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is the particular smell of animal meat such as lamb or goat. The smell of fish or raw food is called '비린내', so the two are kept apart. In cooking people say things like '노린내를 잡다' (to get rid of the gamey smell).

en: to be scorched; to burn; to burn to the bottom of a pot or pan

examples.en: The rice stuck and burned onto the bottom of the pot.

examples.ko: 불을 세게 켜면 고기가 팬에 눌어붙어요.
examples.en: If you turn up the heat, the meat sticks and burns on the pan.

examples.ko: 눌어붙은 찌꺼기를 닦는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to scrub off the burnt-on residue.

examples.ko: 기름을 안 두르면 계란이 눌어붙을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't add oil, the egg can stick and burn.

examples.ko: 국이 눌어붙지 않게 가끔 저어 주세요.
examples.en: Please stir the soup now and then so it doesn't stick and burn.

examples.ko: 냄비에 우유가 눌어붙어서 탄 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: Milk has burned onto the pot, so it smells burnt.

explain: 열 때문에 음식이 그릇에 붙으면서 조금 타는 것을 말해요. '타다'는 많이 까맣게 태우는 느낌이고, '눌어붙다'는 바닥에 딱 붙은 상태에 초점이 있어요. '눌어붙은 밥', '눌은밥'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes food sticking to a pot or pan and slightly burning from heat. '타다' suggests blackened burning, while '눌어붙다' focuses on being stuck to the bottom. You also see '눌어붙은 밥' and '눌은밥'.

en: covered in; a mess of; a thick porridge-like dish

examples.ko: 온몸이 땀 범벅이 되어서 샤워부터 했어요.
examples.en: I was drenched in sweat, so I showered first.
The child's face is covered in chocolate.
I said hello with a tear-streaked face.
My clothes are caked in mud, so I have to do laundry.
I made and ate a pumpkin porridge-like dish.

examples.ko: 거짓말과 소문이 범벅된 이야기라서 믿기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's a story mixed with lies and rumors, so it's hard to believe.

explain: 여러 가지가 마구 섞이거나 뒤덮인 모습을 말해서 '땀 범벅', '눈물 범벅'처럼 다른 명사 뒤에 붙여 많이 써요. 원래는 곡식과 호박 등을 섞어 쑨 음식 이름이에요. 보통 좋지 않은 것이 잔뜩 묻은 상황에 써요.
explain_en: It describes being all mixed up or coated in something, and is usually placed after another noun as in 땀 범벅 or 눈물 범벅. It was originally the name of a dish mixing grains and pumpkin. It usually describes being covered in something unpleasant.

examples.en: My clothes got covered with bread crumbs.
I wiped the crumbs off the desk with a tissue.
The pigeons are pecking at nothing but crumbs.

examples.ko: 부스러기 하나도 남기지 않고 다 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate everything without leaving a single crumb.
When you cut wood, small scraps fly around.

examples.ko: 과자 봉지 바닥에 부스러기밖에 안 남았어요.
examples.en: Only crumbs were left at the bottom of the snack bag.

explain: 과자나 빵이 부서져서 떨어진 작은 조각을 말할 때 가장 자주 써요. '나무 부스러기', '종이 부스러기'처럼 다른 재료에도 써요. '찌꺼기'는 쓰고 남은 더러운 것에 가까워서 느낌이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used most often for the small pieces that fall from broken snacks or bread. It is also used in '나무 부스러기' (wood scraps) and '종이 부스러기' (paper scraps). The similar '찌꺼기' is closer to dirty leftovers after use, so the feeling is different.
